_: THE FIRM'S SETUPS AS ORDINARY DEFINITIONS. TC2000 and TradingView both ship dozens of built-in scans and it is the ONBOARDING PATH, not decoration: a member picks a named setup, gets a WORKING scan, and then EDITS it -- which is how people learn a syntax. A blank formula box loses the wide audience.
_ordinary: EVERY ENTRY IS AN ORDINARY DEFINITION: same store, same `def_hash`, same read-back, editable on arrival. There is no starter flag, no `is_builtin` column and no branch in the save path -- a starter that is special-cased is a second class of object and re-creates the asymmetry spec section 1.1 forbids. This file holds a SOURCE and a frozen TREE; installing one is the member's action through the shipped save path, and the identity is `astHash`'s.
_taxonomy: THE NAMES COME FROM `app/src/constants/setupGroups.js` AND ARE NOT COPIED HERE AS A LIST. This file holds a `source` per setup it can express; the SET of setups and the FAMILY each one belongs to are read from the taxonomy at run time, which is why no entry carries a `family`. A setup with no entry must appear in `_ungrounded` with a reason -- that identity is what makes a NEW setup land RED until somebody decides about it. Two files in this repo carry setup taxonomies and they do not agree: `setupGroups.js` (the labeling taxonomy the Model Book store, the concept vocabulary's attribution check and this file all read) and `app/src/pages/modelbook/setupCatalog.js` (the Setup Library's field-guide, with its own families and its own display names). `setupGroups.js` is authoritative here. Neither count is written down anywhere in this file.
_grounding: GROUNDING IS A LIST OF CITATIONS THAT RESOLVE, AND IT IS RESOLVED RATHER THAN TRUSTED (controller adjudication A-1). Three kinds appear here: `starter_screen` (a screen `saved_screens.py::starters()` ships), `filter_preset` (a labelled threshold in `screener/filters.py::FILTERS`) and `classifier` (a labelled branch of firm code, located by AST). A PLAYBOOK IS NEVER A GROUNDING -- it is prose and cannot mechanically produce a tree -- so the setup name rides as an `attribution`, which this file does not spell either: it is the entry's own KEY.
_no_invented_numbers: EVERY NUMERIC LITERAL IN A STARTER'S TREE MUST BE PUBLISHED BY ONE OF ITS OWN CITATIONS, and every scalar it screens on must be one a citation names. `rs_rank >= 80` is here because the firm ships a preset labelled `Over 80`; 75 would go red NAMING 75. This is the rail that stops a starter from looking like the firm's answer while carrying the catalogue author's opinion.
_no_sentence: NO READ-BACK IS FROZEN HERE, and that is the one place this file deliberately differs from `conceptVocabulary.json`. The card's blurb is `sentenceFor(tree)` in the browser and `sentence_for(tree)` on the server -- derived on every render from the tree that IS the scan. A hand-written blurb would be a second description of one tree and the prose one is the one that drifts (D-A5).
_no_hash: NO `def_hash` IS PRECOMPUTED HERE. The handle is `astHash` over the tree, minted by the shipped save path when a member installs one; a catalogue that carried its own copy would be a second registry and two authorities over one identity.
_ungrounded_rule: A SETUP WITH NO EXPRESSIBLE CONDITION IS NAMED, NOT APPROXIMATED. The member trusts the firm's name on a starter, so a scan that half-means `High Tight Flag` is worse than no scan (AMENDMENT 1's refusal rule, applied to the library). Each reason names its setup and says what is missing -- a column, a published threshold, or the cadence -- because those are three different decisions for the owner. And `rsi(close,14)` is NOT available to close a gap here: E-A9 is open and out of scope, so a setup needing a function the table does not declare stays ungrounded until that phase happens.

_ungrounded.High Tight Flag (Powerplay): High Tight Flag (Powerplay) turns on a PRIOR RUN -- roughly a double in four to eight weeks -- and then a shallow, tight flag on top of it. The table declares `chg_pct_1m` and `pullback_depth_pct`, but the screener publishes no preset on `chg_pct_1m` at all, so the size of the run that makes a flag 'high and tight' is nobody's written-down number. Publish a `chg_pct_1m` preset and this becomes expressible.
_ungrounded.VCP: VCP is the VOLATILITY CONTRACTION pattern, and the contraction SEQUENCE is the tell. The firm's own pattern engine names it `Volatility Contraction Pattern (VCP)` and defines it as successive shallower pullbacks with drying volume into a tight pivot; the Compass coach teaches it as a series of tighter and tighter ranges; the course teaches the scan filter as `recent pullbacks contracting, each swing smaller than the last`. The firm DETECTS exactly that -- `screener/patterns.py::detect_patterns` measures three consecutive ~10-bar swing ranges and emits `vcp` when each is smaller than the last -- but it detects it into `screener_rows.patterns`, a TEXT column, and `closedTable.json` excludes text columns by construction. That is the identical blocker that already refuses `Flat Base Breakout`, and the fix is the same: a per-pattern 0/1 column, not a formula. The nearest declared boolean, `tight_consolidation`, is a DIFFERENT measurement -- the coefficient of variation of the last ten closes, one flat window with no sequence in it -- and the firm's own screen built from it is named `High-RS tight bases`, not VCP. Ship that screen under its own name, or declare a `vcp` column.
_ungrounded.Flat Base Breakout: Flat Base Breakout is a pattern the firm ALREADY DETECTS -- `FILTERS['pattern']` ships a `Flat Base` preset -- but it detects it into `screener_rows.patterns`, a TEXT column, and `closedTable.json` excludes text columns by construction. There is no boolean `flat_base` scalar to screen on, and `pattern_conf_max` carries a confidence with no pattern name attached. The fix is a per-pattern 0/1 column, not a formula.
_ungrounded.IPO Base: IPO Base is defined by how long the symbol has been listed, and the table declares no listing-date or days-since-IPO column. Nothing here can tell a first base from a fourth one.
_ungrounded.Parabolic Short: Parabolic Short is a judgement about the ANGLE of a three-to-five day blow-off and how far it has stretched above its averages. `pct_vs_sma20` and `pct_vs_ema20` are declared, but the only `pct_vs_ema20` preset the firm publishes is `Within 2%` -- a proximity band, the opposite end of the same column -- so the extension that makes a move parabolic is unpublished.
_ungrounded.Parabolic Long: Parabolic Long is the same measurement as Parabolic Short taken from the other side, and it fails for the same reason: no published extension threshold on any `pct_vs_*` column, and no way to say 'the curve is steepening' from one row of a nightly snapshot.
_ungrounded.Wedge Pop: Wedge Pop is trendline GEOMETRY -- a converging upper and lower boundary, then a reclaim through the averages. The closed table declares no trendline, no slope and no wedge flag, and `FILTERS['pattern']` does not detect a wedge either, so there is nothing to cite.
_ungrounded.Wedge Drop: Wedge Drop is Wedge Pop inverted and is ungrounded for the same reason: the converging boundaries that define a wedge exist in no column the table declares and in no pattern the screener detects.
_ungrounded.Episodic Pivot: Episodic Pivot is a gap on a MAJOR CATALYST in a neglected name. The table declares `gap_pct` and `vol_ratio`, so the gap and the volume are expressible -- the catalyst is not. There is no news, filing or earnings-date column, and a scan called Episodic Pivot that returned every 3% gapper would be putting the firm's name on a guess.
_ungrounded.2B Reversal: 2B Reversal turns on a PRIOR EXTREME being broken and not held. Naming that extreme needs a swing lookback -- `lowest(low, N)` or `highest(high, N)` -- and no artifact at the firm publishes an N. The functions exist; the number is nobody's.
_ungrounded.Kicker Candle: Kicker Candle is a TWO-BAR relationship: yesterday closes weak, today gaps up and closes above yesterday's high. `gap_pct` names the gap, but the closed table has no bar-offset node -- `_no_offset` -- so 'yesterday's high' cannot be named, and 'closes weak' has no published threshold.
_ungrounded.News Gappers: News Gappers is the same gap as the firm's own `Gappers holding gains` starter screen (`gap_pct >= 3 && above_50sma`) with one extra claim the table cannot check: that the gap was news-driven. A member scanning News Gappers would get index rebalances and sympathy moves under a name that promised a catalyst. Ship the screen under its own name, or declare a news column.
_ungrounded.4B Setup (Stan Weinstein): 4B Setup (Stan Weinstein) is a STAGE call -- where the symbol sits in Weinstein's four-stage cycle, read off a 30-week line and its slope. The table declares `above_50sma` and `pct_vs_sma200` but no stage label and no moving-average SLOPE, and `screener/technicals.py` labels an MA STACK, not a stage.
_ungrounded.Failed H&S/Rounded Top: Failed H&S/Rounded Top is a pattern that is defined by NOT resolving: everyone sees the top, the breakdown does not come. Naming the neckline needs a swing lookback nobody publishes, and 'the breakdown did not come' needs a bar offset the closed table does not carry.
_ungrounded.Classic U&R: Classic U&R undercuts a PROMINENT PRIOR LOW and reclaims it. `lowest(low, N)` can name a prior low, but which N makes a low prominent is nobody's published number, and the reclaim is a two-bar relationship the table's offset-free grammar cannot state.
_ungrounded.Launchpad: Launchpad's tell is CONVERGENCE, and the closed table cannot say it. The firm's own playbook names the 8-EMA, 21-EMA, 30-SMA and 50-SMA bunched closely together with price consolidating across them, and calls the setup symmetrical: it breaks long or short, and the environment picks the side. The table can say that averages are STACKED, but a stacked and widely SEPARATED trend is the opposite of a coiled bundle, and no artifact at the firm publishes the band that makes a bundle tight. A long-only stack-and-tighten scan would put the firm's name on a different setup. Publish a convergence threshold -- how close the averages must sit to each other -- and this becomes expressible.
_ungrounded.Go Signal: Go Signal is a catalyst gap digesting into a short average and then one wide candle closing above the catalyst high. Both halves fail: there is no catalyst column, and the 9-period average the setup is defined against is not a window any firm artifact publishes.
_ungrounded.HVC: HVC's tell is a LEVEL, and the trade is not the day the level is made. The firm's glossary reads `the highest-volume day's close becomes the line the stock must hold`; the Setup Library calls it `a surge on the highest volume in the lookback, closing strong -- that day's close becomes the pivot price must defend`; and the lesson that teaches it says of the high-volume bar itself `no trade here -- mark the level the day the volume prints, then wait`, with the entry arriving weeks later over the candle that holds the level. Two things are missing. The superlative IS sayable -- `volume >= highest(volume, 252)`, and 252 is the window the firm's own `computeHVC` chart highlight uses -- but `vol_ratio` is a ratio against a 30-day average, so `vol_ratio >= 2` names a common heavy day rather than the highest volume in the lookback, and a level marked on a merely-heavy day is not the one the tape remembers. And naming `that day's close` on a LATER bar needs a bar offset the closed table does not carry (`_no_offset`) -- the same gap that leaves `Kicker Candle`, `Oops Reversal` and `Remount` ungrounded. Publish the lookback as a citable window and the mark-the-level half becomes expressible; the return-and-hold half needs the offset.
_ungrounded.Wick Play: Wick Play is a single-bar discretionary read on where the wick sits relative to the range. `upper_wick_pct` and `lower_wick_pct` ARE declared scalars -- but the screener publishes no preset on either, so every threshold this scan could use would be the catalogue author's. Publish a wick preset and Wick Play becomes expressible in one line.
_ungrounded.Slingshot: Slingshot is defined against the 4-period exponential average OF THE HIGHS. `ema` takes a series, and the closed table declares `high` -- but 4 is not a window any firm artifact publishes, and a starter that picked one would be inventing the setup's own definition.
_ungrounded.Oops Reversal: Oops Reversal gaps BELOW the prior day's low and closes the gap. `gap_pct` publishes `Down >3%`, so the gap down is sayable; 'below the prior day's LOW' and 'closed the gap' both need the previous bar, which the closed table's offset-free grammar cannot name.
_ungrounded.News Failure: News Failure is a headline that does not hold. It needs the headline, and the table declares no news column -- the same gap that leaves News Gappers and Episodic Pivot ungrounded.
_ungrounded.Remount: Remount requires the symbol to have been BELOW its average and to be back above it. `above_50sma` says where it is today; saying where it was yesterday needs a bar offset the closed table does not carry.
_ungrounded.Red to Green: Red to Green turns on the zero line: open below the prior close, close above it. `gap_pct` names the open against the prior close, but the only thresholds the firm publishes on it are +3 and -3, not zero -- and the sweep evaluates the LAST CONFIRMED bar, by which time the intraday transition the setup is named for has already resolved.
_ungrounded.Opening Range Breakout: Opening Range Breakout is an INTRADAY setup and the sweep is a last-confirmed-DAILY-bar screen. Blocked on cadence (design section 8.5), not on vocabulary: the opening range is not a column the nightly snapshot holds.
_ungrounded.Opening Range Breakdown: Opening Range Breakdown is the short side of the same intraday range and is blocked on the same cadence: the sweep runs on the last confirmed daily bar and the snapshot carries no opening range.
_ungrounded.Red to Green (Intraday): Red to Green (Intraday) is explicitly intraday and the sweep is a last-confirmed-DAILY-bar screen. Blocked on cadence (design section 8.5).
_ungrounded.Green to Red: Green to Red is the intraday mirror of Red to Green (Intraday) and is blocked on the same cadence: nothing in a daily snapshot can name a session crossing its own opening reference.
_ungrounded.30min Pivot: 30min Pivot is defined against the first half-hour's high, which exists only on an intraday timeframe. Blocked on cadence (design section 8.5).
_ungrounded.Mean Reversion L/S: Mean Reversion L/S is an INTRADAY setup, and the sweep is a last-confirmed-DAILY-bar screen. Blocked on design section 8.5 (cadence), not on vocabulary.
